title: Pub/Sub fundamentals
description: Sample quiz: delivery guarantees, acknowledgment deadlines, dead-letter handling, and ordering.

questions.question: Which delivery guarantee does a standard Pub/Sub subscription provide by default?

choices.C: Exactly-once delivery for every subscription type

questions.justification: Pub/Sub redelivers a message until it is acknowledged, so a message can arrive more than once. Design subscribers to be idempotent. Exactly-once delivery exists only as an opt-in feature for pull subscriptions, not as the default for every type.

questions.question: A subscriber needs up to 5 minutes to process each message, and Pub/Sub keeps redelivering messages before processing finishes. What is the best fix?

choices.A: Increase the acknowledgment deadline, or have the client library extend the lease while processing
choices.B: Switch the subscription from pull to push
choices.D: Reduce the size of the published messages

questions.justification: Redelivery happens because the message is not acknowledged before the ack deadline expires. Extending the deadline (up to 10 minutes) or letting the client library renew the lease fixes the cause. Changing the delivery type, recreating the subscription, or shrinking messages does not address the deadline.

questions.question: Which settings or features help you handle messages that repeatedly fail processing? (Select all that apply)

choices.B: A retry policy with exponential backoff
choices.C: Topic message retention set to 365 days
choices.D: A maximum delivery attempts value in the dead-letter policy

questions.justification: A dead-letter topic (A) captures messages that cannot be processed, the maximum delivery attempts value (D) decides when a message moves there, and a backoff retry policy (B) spaces out redeliveries. Retention (C) controls how long messages are stored, and the maximum is far below 365 days. Ordering keys (E) control sequence, not failure handling.

questions.question: Messages for the same customer must be processed in the order they were published. What should you configure?

choices.A: Set an ordering key on each message and enable message ordering on the subscription
choices.D: Use a larger machine type for the subscriber

questions.justification: Pub/Sub orders messages that share an ordering key when message ordering is enabled on the subscription. Using the customer ID as the key keeps each customer's messages in sequence while still allowing parallelism across customers.
